rules: Spoken words, private thoughts, and hidden motives are stored separately.
NPC dialogue is generated from personality, goals, knowledge, relationship, stress, and context.
Characters may refuse to answer, redirect, joke, flatter, threaten, or remain silent.
Dialogue cannot reveal facts the speaker does not know.

152_DECEPTION_AND_TRUTH_SYSTEM.json.resolution: contested check only when uncertainty materially matters
rules: A successful lie does not rewrite reality.
A failed detection check does not prove the lie true.
Evidence can override social rolls.
Experienced actors may use polished partial truths rather than simple lies.

hard_limits: A roll cannot force an NPC to violate a core value without extraordinary leverage.
A roll cannot make an NPC forget known evidence.
Intimidation may secure compliance while reducing trust.
Negotiation requires something each side values.

rules: Strong emotional memories persist longer.
Memory intensity can fade while factual belief remains.
Trauma does not create perfect recall.
Repeated experiences can reinforce or overwrite expectations without deleting history.
Reputation is collective belief, not objective truth.
Different communities can hold contradictory reputations of the same person.
Reputation changes through witnessed events, credible reports, records, media, and rumors.
Private relationships remain separate from public image.
Cues are probabilistic, culturally mediated, and context-dependent.
No single cue proves deception.
Fatigue, illness, fear, neurodiversity, training, and injury can mimic deceptive cues.
Highly trained characters may control some signals but not all physiological responses.

157_SOCIAL_OBSERVATION_ENGINE.json.rule: Observation produces hypotheses unless direct evidence exists; narration must distinguish the two.

rules: Conversation context persists across scenes when remembered.
Promises and threats can become future obligations.
Repeated contradiction increases suspicion.
NPCs may intentionally revisit old statements.
Rumors retain lineage to their originating claim.
Multiple independent sources increase credibility only if actually independent.
An official denial may reduce or amplify spread depending on trust.
